quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before starting the motorcycle
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before you start your motorcycle. Adjust them so you can see the lane behind you and the lane next to you.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you turn or change lanes. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for traffic around your motorcycle before changing lanes.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to driving a car. However:

options.text: Being seen is more important on a motorcycle than in a car.
Being seen is less important on a motorcycle than in a car.
You should pass on the shoulder instead of the main road.
You must make eye contact with other drivers when riding a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Being seen is more important on a motorcycle than in a car.
questions.explanation: Being seen is more critical on a motorcycle. Motorcycles are smaller and can easily hide in another vehicle's blind spot. Other drivers may not notice you even if they look.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: Don't help improve how visible you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Brightly-colored helmets are recommended. They protect you in a crash and make it easier for other road users to see you.

questions.question: When being passed, you should not move to the far side of your lane because it:

options.text: Stops the other driver from pulling back too early.
Causes the other driver to pull back too early.
Makes the other driver pass you faster.
Encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes the other driver to pull back too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane could cause the other driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve, do them separately. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either the front or rear brake, not both.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: To make a quick stop on wet pavement, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes for a quick stop on slippery surfaces. Apply the front brake gradually to prevent it from locking.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, it is usually best to:

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the road's edge.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the road's edge.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip both handlebars firmly. Ease off the throttle and keep the motorcycle straight. If you must brake, gradually apply the brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: If you must ride over an object in the road, you should not:

options.text: Slow down before reaching the object.
Keep your motorcycle straight up and down.
Speed up as you approach the object.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up as you approach the object.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid hitting an object, slow down first. Keep your motorcycle straight up and down. Rise slightly off your seat so your joints can absorb the impact and prevent you from being thrown off.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, it should have all of the following qualities, except:

options.text: Meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is attractive.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When a rider's left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means the rider:
questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of mechanical turn signals. A left arm extended straight out to the left means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: A car is entering the highway from an entrance ramp on your right and may not see your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left side of your lane so they can share the lane if needed.
Move into another lane if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of space to vehicles entering the highway from an entrance ramp. Move to a lane farther from the entrance ramp if possible. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to give them room to safely enter the highway.

questions.question: An experienced rider:

options.text: Changes position within their lane based on road and traffic conditions.
Stays in the same spot in the lane at all times.
Weaves within the lane to be more visible.
Travels only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes position within their lane based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle rider has three lane position choices. The rider should pick the safest position based on the road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, your motorcycle must have all of the following, except:

options.text: A seat big enough for two people.
Properly adjusted lights, mirrors, and tires.
A sign on the back saying a passenger is riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sign on the back saying a passenger is riding.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle needs a seat large enough for two people and foot pegs for the passenger. Adjust your motorcycle to handle the extra weight of a passenger.

questions.question: To best control a motorcycle, a rider should:

options.text: Use arms to hold their body up.
Keep knees away from the gas tank.
Keep feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle, not hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain balance.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids from braking, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake immediately and re-apply it smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately and re-apply it smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks from braking, release the front brake right away and re-apply it smoothly.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Approach it slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach it slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases your motorcycle, downshift and approach the dog slowly. Once you are close, accelerate and leave it behind. Do not try to kick it.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A danger of braking too hard is:

options.text: Losing traction on one or both wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can cause you to lose traction on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: What shape is a speed limit sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular. They are white with black lettering. These signs tell you the traffic rules you must follow.

questions.question: What is a motorcycle horn useful for?

options.text: Usually cannot be heard by others.
Can be used to get someone's attention quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be used to get someone's attention quickly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle horn can help you get someone's attention fast. However, a motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn. Other drivers may not hear it. Do not rely only on your horn to avoid danger.

questions.question: Where should you ride when being passed?

options.text: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Weave among the three portions of the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle raises your risk of a crash. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too early and unsafely.

questions.question: The body removes one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are left in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the number of drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining in the body.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Arrange for a safe ride home for your friend.
Occupy your friend with activities to distract them from drinking.
Keep your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Do not let your friend ride a motorcycle while impaired. You can help by arranging another ride home, keeping them busy with other activities, and preventing them from leaving until they are sober. Ask other friends to help stop them.
